ing: about 8 oz, thinly sliced, for the side
st: Make the greens first: heat the oil in a pan, cook the onion until soft, about 4 minutes, then add the tomatoes and cook 5 minutes until saucy.
Add the collard greens and a splash of water. Cover and cook until tender, about 10 minutes. Keep warm.
Bring [[3 cups]] water and the salt to a boil in a heavy pot.
Mix [[0.5 cup]] cornmeal with [[1 cup]] cold water in a bowl until smooth. Whisk it into the boiling water and cook for 3 minutes to form a thin porridge.
Turn the heat to low. Add the remaining cornmeal a handful at a time, stirring hard with a wooden spoon so no lumps form.
Keep pressing and stirring the mass against the side of the pot until it is thick, smooth and pulls away from the pot, about 5 minutes.
Cover and let it steam on very low heat for 3 minutes.
Shape into a mound with a wet spoon, slice into wedges, and serve with the greens. Eat with your hands, pinching off pieces to scoop up the greens.

ing: ribs or bone-in chunks; beef short ribs also work
st: Rub the meat with the garlic, oil, salt, pepper and the juice of 1 lemon. Marinate in the fridge for at least 1 hour.
Heat a grill for two-zone cooking: coals on one side, meat on the other. Aim for medium-low heat around 300°F (150°C).
Lay the meat on the cooler side, cover the grill, and cook, turning every 20 minutes.
Move the meat over direct heat for the last 5 minutes per side to char and crisp the outside. It should reach at least 145°F (63°C) and be tender.
While it cooks, mix the onions, tomatoes, chili, cilantro and the juice of 1 lemon with a pinch of salt for the side.
Rest the meat for 10 minutes, then chop into bite-sized pieces on a board.
Serve with the onion and tomato side, plus ugali if you like.

ing: about 1.5 lb, stems removed, thinly sliced
st: Wash the collard greens well, stack the leaves, roll them up and slice into thin ribbons.
Heat the oil in a large pan over medium heat. Cook the onion until soft and golden, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds, then add the tomatoes. Cook until they break down into a soft sauce, about 5 minutes.
Add the greens in handfuls, stirring as they wilt. Pour in [[0.25 cup]] water and add the salt.
Cover and cook, stirring now and then, until tender but still bright green, about 8 minutes.
Taste, adjust the salt and serve hot with ugali or rice.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and turmeric and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and cook until they turn jammy, about 6 minutes.
Stir in the potatoes, carrots, beans, corn, salt and [[3 cups]] water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat, cover and simmer until the vegetables are tender and the stew has thickened.
Mash a few beans and potatoes against the side of the pot to thicken it, then simmer 5 more minutes.
Taste for salt, top with cilantro and serve hot.

ing: chopped; spinach or kale if pumpkin leaves are not available
st: Put the potatoes in a pot, cover with cold water, add [[1 tsp]] salt and bring to a boil. Cook until very soft.
In the last 5 minutes, add the peas and corn to the pot.
Melt [[1 tbsp]] butter in a pan and cook the onion until soft, about 4 minutes. Add the greens and cook until wilted, about 3 minutes.
Drain the potatoes, peas and corn well, saving a splash of the cooking water.
Mash everything together with the remaining [[2 tbsp]] butter and the warm milk until mostly smooth with some corn and peas still whole.
Fold in the cooked greens and onion and the remaining [[0.5 tsp]] salt. The mash should turn green. Add a splash of the cooking water if it is stiff.
Serve hot as a side with stew or grilled meat.
Put the beef in a pot with [[2 cups]] water, [[1 tsp]] salt and half of the garlic. Simmer, covered, until nearly tender. Strain and save the broth.
Heat the oil in a wide heavy pot over medium heat. Add the cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, peppercorns and cumin, stirring for 30 seconds.
Add the onions and cook, stirring often, until deep brown, about 20 minutes. Do not rush this step, since it gives the pilau its color.
Stir in the remaining garlic and ginger, then add the beef and brown it for 5 minutes.
Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes to coat. Pour in the beef broth topped up with water to make [[4 cups]], plus [[1 tsp]] salt.
Bring to a boil, then cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender. Make sure the beef is fully tender.
Rest off the heat for 10 minutes, then fluff with a fork and serve with kachumbari.

ing: divided, for the dough, layers and pan
st: Mix the flour, sugar and salt in a large bowl. Rub in [[3 tbsp]] oil with your fingers.
Stir in the warm milk, then add warm water a little at a time until a soft dough forms.
Knead on a floured surface for 8 minutes until smooth and stretchy. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Divide the dough into 8 balls. Roll one into a thin circle and brush lightly with oil.
Roll the circle up into a long rope, then coil it into a snail shape and tuck the end under. Repeat with all the balls, then rest 10 minutes.
Roll each coil flat into a circle about 7 inches wide.
Heat a dry skillet over medium heat. Cook a chapati for about 1 minute until it begins to bubble, then flip.
Brush with oil, flip again and cook until golden spots form on both sides, about 2 minutes total. Stack in a cloth to keep soft.
Warm the coconut milk until just lukewarm. Stir in the yeast and [[1 tbsp]] of the sugar and let it sit for 5 minutes until foamy.
In a large bowl, mix the flour, remaining sugar, cardamom and salt.
Pour in the yeast mixture and stir to make a soft dough. Knead for 5 minutes until smooth.
Cover and let rise in a warm place until doubled in size.
Roll out the dough on a floured surface to about 0.5 inch thick. Cut into triangles or squares.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the pieces in small batches, turning once, until puffed and golden brown, about 3 minutes.
Drain on paper towels. Serve warm or at room temperature with tea.
Slice the red onion as thinly as you can. Soak it in cold water for 5 minutes, then drain well to mellow its bite.
Dice the tomatoes and place them in a bowl.
Add the drained onion, cilantro and chili.
Pour over the lime juice and sprinkle in the salt. Toss gently.
Let it sit for 10 minutes so the flavors blend.
Taste and add more salt or lime if needed. Serve cold with grilled meat or pilau.
Put the potatoes in a pot with enough water to cover and [[1 tsp]] salt. Bring to a boil and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the peas and corn and cook until the potatoes are fork tender, about 8 more minutes.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a pan and cook the onion until soft, about 5 minutes. Add the spinach and cook until wilted, about 2 minutes.
Drain the vegetables, keeping a little of the cooking water.
Return them to the pot with the onion and spinach and the remaining [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Mash roughly with a potato masher until the mixture is thick and green, adding a splash of the cooking water if too dry.
Serve hot with nyama choma or stew.
